subject: Dedicated capacity ramp: GPU procurement timeline & vendor action items
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask from Acme — planning note

Team,

Quick internal note before I loop vendors in: Acme just committed to a 12-month Dedicated deployment targeting a go-live window in mid-June. They indicated an initial throughput target equivalent to ~120 concurrent chat sessions at p95 < 400ms, which we mapped to roughly 48 H100-equivalent GPUs under our preferred replication/batching assumptions.

Key constraints we need to drive on procurement/VPC reservations: 
- OEM lead times: H100/A100 procurement quotes will likely be 12–20 weeks with partial frontload options; confirm swap and acceptance windows.
- Cloud reservations: if we rely on AWS/GCP capacity for burst or DR, we must secure regional capacity reservations now (us-west-2 preferred).
- Staged delivery: propose a three-phased ramp (25% pilot, 50% mid-ramp, 100% production).

Action for this morning: I will send a short vendor email thread to Evan (NVIDIA OEM) and Priya (AWS partner rep). Rishi/Vivek — please scan the attached RDW-hw-specs-req-2026Q2.pdf and call out any adjustments to counts or fallback model variants (e.g., mix of 80GB H100 + some 40GB A100 nodes).

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-hw-specs-req-2026Q2.pdf (specs + assumptions)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@nvidia-oem.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: GPU delivery windows & cloud reservations for RDW-DEAL-2026-045

Evan / Priya —

Following up from our internal planning: Acme Analytics (see Sam cc'd below) has an approved budget and is targeting mid-June for production on Redwood Dedicated. We need to align on firm delivery/availability timelines and options for staged delivery. High-level asks: 

1) OEM (Evan): Please confirm earliest possible ship windows for H100 80GB and A100 40GB assemblies under a 48-GPU equivalent requirement. Do you support partial shipments (e.g., 12 units in 4–6 weeks, remainder 8–12 weeks)? What are lead time ranges under standard PO vs. expedited pricing? Any long-lead components (PSUs, mezzanine cards) we should expect backorders on?

2) Cloud partner (Priya): If we reserve capacity at AWS in us-west-2, can AWS commit to a reservation hold for the quantities equivalent to 48 GPUs (or a hybrid: 24 dedicated HW + 24 reserved cloud GPUs) for the June window? What are the billing/commit implications and termination clauses?

3) Joint ask: Customs/freight cushion — realistic ETA from PO to on-site acceptance for OEM shipments to our colo or customer-hosted sites (include customs clearance typical durations).

We attached a short mutual action plan and our HW spec assumptions. Sam — looping you so your SRE/infra leads can weigh in if they prefer cloud-only vs. hybrid.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: 20260227-Acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Evan Li <evan.li@nvidia-oem.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: GPU delivery windows & cloud reservations for RDW-DEAL-2026-045

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks for the details. High-level:
- Current lead times: For H100 80GB modules under an OEM program we are seeing ~16–18 weeks typical, A100 40GB ~10–14 weeks. Expedited lanes (premium pricing) can shave ~3–4 weeks depending on allocation at order time.
- Partial shipments: Supported. We can frontload up to 30% of units within 6–8 weeks if PO and deposit are in place and stock is available at allocation time. We recommend a 3-stage PO (pilot, mid, final) with explicit shipment windows and deposit schedule.
- Long-lead risks: High-capacity PSUs and certain optics for PCIe fabrics are the main risk items. We'll flag those on the quote and propose alternatives if lead times extend.
- Customs/freight: Ship-to-US colo sites currently average 7–14 days in transit + customs clearance 3–7 days depending on HS codes. Plan for 3–5 business days of final on-site staging and burn-in.

I'll attach a preliminary OEM quote and proposed PO schedule; can confirm stock allocations early next week once you share required part numbers and a two-week deposit window.

Regards,
Evan Li
OEM Sales — Systems
NVIDIA OEM Solutions

Attachment: NV-OEM-prelim-quote-0303.pdf
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aws-partner.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU delivery windows & cloud reservations for RDW-DEAL-2026-045

Hi Marissa,

We can reserve capacity in us-west-2 for a planned June ramp but need a firm commitment by March 16 to lock instance reservations for P4/H100-style SKUs. Reservation options: 
- Standard savings plan (12-month) with capacity reservation add-on — will guarantee instance availability but requires the minimum commit.
- Short-term capacity hold: 30–60 day hold for a premium (useful for hybrid bursts).

Billing notes: reserved instances show up as a mixed billing line; termination before 12 months requires a release fee or transfer. We recommend the hybrid approach Evan outlined: frontload OEM hardware for pilot traffic and keep cloud capacity as a burst/backstop.

If you send me the exact count mix (H100 vs A100) and the go-live staging dates, I can generate an invoice and reservation contract for legal.

Best,
Priya Shah
Strategic Partnerships, AWS
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evan Li <evan.li@nvidia-oem.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aws-partner.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp: GPU procurement timeline & vendor action items

Sam — short executive summary and next steps so we have alignment across procurement and SRE: 

Summary: 
- OEM (NVIDIA) can support partial shipments; expected lead time for production H100s is ~16 weeks. They can frontload ~30% within 6–8 weeks with deposit.
- Cloud partner (AWS) can reserve capacity in us-west-2 if we provide counts by 2026-03-16; 12-month reservations or short-term holds are options.
- Customs/freight + on-site staging adds ~2–4 weeks to OEM deliveries in practice.

Proposed ramp & immediate asks (mutual action plan attached):
1) By 2026-03-10 (Marissa/Rishi) — finalize part numbers and confirm hybrid counts (we propose 32 H100-equivalent + 16 A100-equivalent as a balanced mix).
2) By 2026-03-12 (Acme procurement) — deposit approval for pilot PO (covering 25% of hardware).
3) By 2026-03-16 (Marissa/Priya) — provision reservation contract from AWS for burst capacity covering remaining peak load.
4) By 2026-04-01 (Redwood infra) — acceptance test plan (SLA, burn-in, monitoring hooks) and delivery checklist.

Risks/notes: Customs changes or allocation shifts at the OEM could push final completion to late July. If Acme needs a hard mid-June cutoff, we should escalate to OEM allocation team and consider a larger cloud buffer.

Sam — any constraints on your side to the dates above? If everything looks good I will issue the pilot PO template to Evan (cc'd) and share the AWS reservation contract once Priya generates it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20260227-Acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
